headline: 17 killed in mob violence across Bangladesh in July, HRSS report
summary: A Human Rights Support Society report reveals a surge in mob violence and domestic abuse, alongside a decline in political violence during the month.
details: At least 17 people were killed and 51 injured in mob violence across the country in July, according to the Human Rights Support Society (HRSS).
Six people died and 164 others were injured in 45 incidents of political violence, while political violence declined compared to June.
The report highlights a severe toll of domestic violence, with 45 women killed and 23 others dying by suicide after abuse.
Child abuse was also widespread, with 34 children dying and 146 others suffering physical or mental harm.
Workplace safety remains a critical issue, as 55 workers died in accidents due to unsafe conditions and lack of protective equipment.
The HRSS report also noted that 23 workers were killed in 79 incidents of violence against workers.
Regarding freedom of expression, 55 journalists faced abuse in 36 incidents, and several others were detained or faced cases.
Additionally, three people died in custody, including two in police custody and one under the Detective Branch.

headline_marked: Saudi Crown Prince [[urges Trump not to attack Iran]]
headline: Saudi Crown Prince urges Trump not to attack Iran
summary: Mohammed bin Salman warns that a major US strike on Iranian energy facilities could escalate a five-month conflict into a more devastating war.
details: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) has called on US President Donald Trump to refrain from launching a major military strike against Iran, according to sources.
The request follows reports that Trump is considering attacks on Iran's energy-related facilities in response to missile strikes on a US base in Jordan and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.
MBS expressed concern during a telephone call on Saturday, warning that such an escalation could make the ongoing five-month conflict significantly more severe.
Iran has already warned that any US attack would be met with retaliatory strikes targeting energy and critical infrastructure in Israel and Gulf nations.
Saudi Arabia's Defense Minister, Prince Khalid bin Salman, also met with Trump and Vice President JD Vance to emphasize Riyadh's position in favor of de-escalation.
Other regional powers, including Qatar, the UAE, Turkey, and Pakistan, are also urging both Washington and Tehran to reduce tensions.
Meanwhile, Qatari mediators are working with US and Omani officials to resume shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, though the outcome remains uncertain.
caption:
A major US strike on Iran could trigger a devastating regional war. Saudi Arabia is now urging Donald Trump to step back.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) has called on US President Donald Trump to refrain from launching a major military strike against Iran, according to sources.

The request follows reports that Trump is considering attacks on Iran's energy-related facilities in response to missile strikes on a US base in Jordan and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

MBS expressed concern during a telephone call on Saturday, warning that such an escalation could make the ongoing five-month conflict significantly more severe.

Iran has already warned that any US attack would be met with retaliatory strikes targeting energy and critical infrastructure in Israel and Gulf nations.

Saudi Arabia's Defense Minister, Prince Khalid bin Salman, also met with Trump and Vice President JD Vance to emphasize Riyadh's position in favor of de-escalation.

Other regional powers, including Qatar, the UAE, Turkey, and Pakistan, are also urging both Washington and Tehran to reduce tensions.

Meanwhile, Qatari mediators are working with US and Omani officials to resume shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, though the outcome remains uncertain.
